To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amino acid residue Y5 in the N-terminal domain of the Gyr B subunit of DNA topoisomerase II is essential for the expression of gyrase activity in vivo.

Y5S and Y5F mutant gyrase B subunits, but not the N-terminal domain-deletion mutants of the same proteins, are deficient in vivo for DNA supercoiling activity and compete with the wild-type GyrB subunt for the maintenance of plasmids.
the Y5-mutated GyrB protein is deficient in vivo and in vitro for DNA gyrase activities and that the Y5 amino acid is a crucial residue in GyrB for expression of the gyrae B activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the amino acid residues of the DNA gyrase B protein which are essential for the in vivo expression and activity of the gyrase.
the identification of the structural and/or functional domains of the GyrAB complex that may be involved in the regulation of DNA gyrase activity and plasmid copy numbers in vivo.
the study of the expression and the in vitro and in vivo activities of DNA gyrase B mutants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Y5 is essential for the in vivo expression of the gyral activity of DNA gyrase.
the amino acid at position 5 in the N-terminal domain of GyrB subdomain is crucial for the expression of GyrB activity in vivo.
the Y5 residue is crucial for the expression of DNA gyrase activity and that this amino acid is not essential for the expression of a GyrB fragment containing only the 43-kDa ATPase domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Y5 amino acid is crucial for DNA gyrase B activity, and that the C-terminal domain of GyrB is important for plasmid maintenance in vivo.
the Y5S and Y5F mutations affect the expression of the DNA gyrase B activity, but not that of its N-terminal ATPase domain.
the N-terminal fragment of GyrB sub-unit can be expressed in bacteria, but that the C-terminal fragment cannot.
